decisive_items: Small red node and mild joint deformity at distal interphalangeal joint of left index finger
Hebreden node at DIP of the left index finger of the case
response.rationale: Psoriatic Arthritis is the most likely diagnosis due to the presence of a Hebreden node and joint deformity at the DIP joint, along with morning stiffness and multiple joint involvement. While Rheumatoid Arthritis is a close contender, the negative RF and normal anti-CCP antibodies contradict this diagnosis.

rejected.why: Osteoarthritis is less likely due to the presence of morning stiffness, which is not typical for this condition.
Spondyloarthritis is a broader category that includes Psoriatic Arthritis, but the specific symptoms and findings in this case make Psoriatic Arthritis a more specific diagnosis.

SARS-CoV-2 related arthritis is possible, but the temporal relationship between the infection and symptom onset, as well as the presence of a Hebreden node, make Psoriatic Arthritis a more likely diagnosis.

Post-vaccination Reactive Arthritis is a possibility, but the presence of a Hebreden node and joint deformity at the DIP joint, along with morning stiffness and multiple joint involvement, make Psoriatic Arthritis a more specific diagnosis.
